# dsh-conversation-links
**English** | 简体中文
Bring the record of one DSH conversation into another: mention it with `@`, drag it in from the side
bar, or open a conversation, tick a few of its messages and insert them somewhere else.
## Install
Either route works; reload the DSH page afterwards (`Ctrl+R` in the desktop app):
**From a GitHub Release** (no clone needed):

Download `dsh-conversation-links-<version>.tgz` from the latest release,
extract it to get the `pack
age/` directory, then:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
**From source**:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Uninstall: `plugin_manager action=set_bundle target=dsh-conversation-links enabled=false`.

> It is also published on npm (`npm i dsh-conversation-links`), but DSH's `install_bundle`
> takes a

n **absolute directory path**, so point it at `node_modules/dsh-conversation-links`
> when installin
g from npm. Everything else is the same.
## Usage
There are three ways to use it.
### 1. Mention another conversation with `@`

Type `@` in the composer: the candidate panel first lists "Files & folders", then a
"Conversations"

group (the `@conversation-link` source this plugin registers). Picking a
conversation inserts a conv

ersation chip into the composer; on send, the host attaches a
read-only snapshot of that conversatio
n as a separate user message (`## Referenced sessions`).

> **Why this plugin registers its own `@` source:** the built-in DSH source
> (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-cli

ent-ui-reference`) asks the host remote
> `sessionReferenceResolver.candidates` for its conversation

candidates, and handles failure
> as `result.ok ? result.value : []` — one remote error **silently

degrades to an empty
> array**. File candidates still render, so `@` shows only "Files & folders" an

d no
> conversations at all (that is exactly what happened on this machine). This plugin's
> `@conve

rsation-link` source reads the client-side session list (`sessions.list`) instead
> and does not dep

end on the host remote, so the group can no longer vanish silently.
>
> Both sources insert the same

wire format, `@title`, so it is
> fully compatible with a hand-typed `@` and with DSH's own referen

ce chips. Snapshot
> injection on send is still done by the built-in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-refer

ence`;
> this plugin does not reimplement it.
Implementation notes (read before touching this code):

- `candidates(projection, { query, quoted, drilled, signal })` **must return a Promise / be
declared

`async`**: the trigger controller does `source.candidates(...).then(...)`, and a
synchronous array

throws — the whole group then disappears without a trace.
- Each candidate carries its own `section`

(`t("sectionSessions")` → "Conversations"), which
together with `showGroupTitle: false` forms its o

wn group.
- `onPick` must return `{ insert: { source, ref, label, appearance: "session", clipboardTe

xt } }`
to insert a real chip; returning `{ text }` only inserts the raw wire text (the editor does

not decorate it into a chip live).
- Register with `ctx.inject(["inputTriggers"], ...)` + `owner.eff

ect(() => triggers.registerSource(...))`,
[该节后续省略]
### 2. Drag a conversation from the sidebar into the composer

Press and hold a conversation row in the sidebar, drag it onto any conversation's composer,
and rele

s and hold a conversation row in the sidebar, drag it onto any conversation's composer,
and release:

- the composer shows a dashed highlight while you drag over it;
- on release, a reference chip for t

hat conversation is inserted into that composer;
- the drag itself is still DSH's original "reorder

workspaces" drag — this plugin only
listens in the capture phase and does not change the original be

es" drag — this plugin only
listens in the capture phase and does not change the original behaviour.
### 3. Open the picker and tick the messages you want
Two entry points:

- **the "conversation reference" button at the left of the composer** (`conversation.input.left`,
or

der 40) — the source conversation defaults to the current one and can be switched;
- **the inline bu

tton on a sidebar row while hovering it** (`sidebar.workspaces.session.row.action`,
order 500) — use
s that conversation as the source directly.
Panel layout:

- Left column: a search box + the source conversation list (current conversation / all
conversations

, newest first, archived last);
- Right column: that conversation's messages (user / assistant, filt

ered by DSH's own
projection rules: tool calls, system messages, subagent messages and blank message

s are
skipped; compaction checkpoints are kept). Tick any of them; "Select all / Clear",
"Load older

messages" and expand / collapse for long messages are supported;
[该节后续省略]
## Known limitations

1. When the target is another conversation, the messages land in **that conversation's
persisted dra

ft**, not in its live editor (DSH only binds a draft writer to mounted
conversations). Open that con

versation to see it, then send when ready.
2. Dragging relies on native HTML5 DnD and does not work

on touch devices (use the two button
entry points there).
3. Records are read through `sessions.reta

in()` + `eventSource`, with no extra host HTTP route;
the host half of this plugin (`lib/index.js`)

is therefore an empty implementation and all
logic lives on the client.
4. What gets inserted is a *

*text snapshot**, not a live link; later changes to the target
conversation do not flow back.
## Compatibility

- DSH `>= 0.2.0-rc.2`, Node `>= 18`, Web platform (`dsh.client.platform = "web"`).
- DSH internals u

sed (all public client services / slots — please open an issue if an upgrade
breaks them): `conversa

tion.input.shell(id)`, `shell.actions.captureInsertion/insertText/setDraft`,
`sessions.retain/list`,

`inputTriggers.registerSource`, `slots.inject/register`,
`uiSession.current`. DOM selectors: `[data

-row-key^="session:"]` (sidebar rows),
`[data-composer-card]` / `[data-composer-seat]` / `[data-conv

ersation-region="composer"]`
(the composer), `[data-conversation-session]` (DOM → session id).
